first_impression.reaction: OK, the first paragraph actually answers me: it's not automatic, and I probably need to add it to a policy. That's what I came for. The key takeaways sit right under the intro, which is good on my phone. One wobble: it's all Australian, and I'm reading this in Singapore. I'd skim the takeaways and the FAQ, then probably bookmark it for the checklist table.

journey.quote: Engagement ring insurance is not automatic.
journey.reaction: Good. Straight answer in the first few lines, no story about a couple in Positano first.

journey.quote: This guide follows the ring from the counter to a proposal abroad and on to the wedding, using only public Australian sources.
journey.reaction: Ah, so it's Australian. I'm in Singapore. Some of this still applies, but the AFCA and Moneysmart bits won't help me. I'd like to know that before I scroll too far, and I nearly do.

journey.quote: Travel insurance often caps each valuable item and rarely pays for theft of anything left unattended, so it is not a substitute for jewellery cover.
journey.reaction: This is the one thing I didn't know. I'd assumed travel insurance would cover it. Useful.

journey.section: What the PDS is, and why it matters
journey.quote: A PDS is the document a provider must give you when it offers a financial product.
journey.reaction: Right after the takeaways I land in a definitions section. On the train I'd scroll past this. It feels like a speed bump before the actual 'three ways' part.

journey.section: Three ways to insure an engagement ring in Australia
journey.quote: There are three places a ring can sit: your home contents policy, a separate policy for valuables, or travel insurance while you are away.
journey.reaction: Clear and scannable. This is the section I'd actually read.

journey.section: What to check in any policy before you rely on it
journey.quote: | Is loss covered, as well as theft and damage? | PDS, list of insured events |
journey.reaction: The table is the bit I'd screenshot. Practical, easy to read on a phone.

journey.section: What to check in any policy before you rely on it
journey.quote: Where a source does not say how jewellery cover works, the honest answer is to check your policy.
journey.reaction: Honest, I'll give it that. But after a few 'ask your insurer' lines I start to feel the page is sending me elsewhere for the real answer.

journey.quote: ### Does travel insurance cover my engagement ring overseas?
journey.reaction: The FAQ questions match exactly what I'd type into Google. If I jumped straight here I'd get most of what I need.

journey.section: Travelling to your destination wedding with the rings
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, so the logistics around the rings sit inside one plan.
journey.reaction: Bit of a jump from insurance to a wedding planner pitch. It's short, so it doesn't bother me much, but I'm not here for that.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how much does engagement ring insurance cost? Even a general sense of what drives the premium would help.
Is any of this relevant if I'm not in Australia? What should someone in Singapore or elsewhere look at?
When was this written or last checked? I want to know it's still true in 2026.
Does a new ring get picked up by my contents policy automatically for a while, or not at all?

turn_offs_found.quote: This guide follows the ring from the counter to a proposal abroad and on to the wedding, using only public Australian sources.
turn_offs_found.why: The Australia-only scope is only clear in the intro body, not the title, so a non-Australian searcher invests time before realising half the specifics don't apply to them.

turn_offs_found.quote: A PDS is the document a provider must give you when it offers a financial product.
turn_offs_found.why: A definitions block sits between the takeaways and the actual answer section, which slows a skim reader on a phone.

would_share_with: My fiancé, just the checklist table and the travel section before our trip

cta_reaction.quote: See [how a Wedded Advisor plans the wedding travel](/wonderland-concierge).
cta_reaction.why: I came for an insurance answer, not a planner. I don't know the brand yet. I might bookmark the page, but I wouldn't click through to a planning service from here.

top_3_changes: Make the Australian scope obvious up top (title or first line), with one sentence for readers elsewhere, e.g. that the checklist questions apply to any policy.
Move the 'What the PDS is' definitions below the 'Three ways' section, or fold them into a one-line note, so the answer comes straight after the takeaways.
Show a visible 'last updated' date so a searcher knows the information is current.
